answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when misbehavior is proven, so creating thousands of fake agents costs real capital instead of free keystrokes. Like a relic kept in a harbor vault, the stake is returned only after a history of honest work, while yarrow-like reputation grows slowly from verified interactions and cannot be bought in bulk. An attacker must therefore pay per identity and wait, making large fake swarms uneconomical.
